title: scenarios: a build-over-the-draft-door mode, and with it a measured answer to how much hosted rule text is still needed
body:
epic:#34659#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnXJdSZifpEN5i7aU

Filing gate: ④ a child of the cross-lane parent #34659 (the 「MCP 二期与问数」 epic), filed on the maintainer's word in this seat's chat, 2026-11-17, verbatim: 「三点都同意，按最终计划把后续里程碑的卡全部立出来」, and, on the list of thirteen cards the seat then showed: 「同意」. The ruling records are #34659 comment 6940528935 and #34691 comment 6943107981. Readings: objectstack `a0326b06`, cloud `53a5844`, 2026-11-17.

## Why

Whether the draft door stages working apps, and whether the rule text the hosted product still serves earns its place, are both open questions that only a build run can answer. Today the audit of that rule text is a reading of the code, not a measurement.

Who acts: the devx lane (`packages/qa/scenarios`). Reader: the eval seat, and the maintainer when the hosted rule text is cut.

## Evidence

- The scenario runner builds through local project files only; no mode builds through MCP.
- No build-accuracy eval drives the hosted MCP door either.
- The rule-by-rule audit of the hosted corpus judged 15 of 60 rules already covered by a check; that judgement was not tested by removing them.

## Scope

- A runner mode in which the authoring client has the draft door's tools and the published skills, and no project files; the build is graded as today after a person-equivalent publish step.
- Arms: with and without the build skill; with and without a named set of rule texts, so a rule's removal can be measured.

## Done when

- One round at five repetitions per arm is on record as an `eval-run`.

## Relations
